checks.claim: Mercedes S-Class rear-axle steering turns the rear wheels up to 10 degrees and cuts the turning circle by up to about 2 meters
checks.why: Mercedes' S-Class (W223) press text, reposted on a forum, gives a maximum rear steering angle of 10° and a turning circle reduced by up to 2 m. Autoevolution confirms a reduction of 6.5 ft (2 m). The system is optional.

sources.title: Mercedes-Benz Revolutionizes Rear-wheel Steering in the 2021 S-Class - autoevolution

checks.claim: On the Mercedes S-Class, the rear wheels turn opposite the front below about 60 km/h (37 mph) and the same way above that
checks.why: Motor1 and Mercedesblog both state the opposite direction up to 60 km/h (37 mph) and the same direction above; CarExpert agrees.

sources.title: 2023 Mercedes GLC Spied Putting Rear-Wheel Steering To Work
The new Mercedes S-Class W223 received rear axle steering and E-Active body control suspension
Rear wheel steering: What is it?

checks.claim: Some rear-steer systems, such as BMW's Integral Active Steering and one DAF truck rear axle, are designed so a fault leaves the rear wheels centred or straight
checks.why: Evidence is limited to a DAF case study and a parts-retailer page on BMW; no general rule and no Mercedes source, so it can't be claimed for all systems or the S-Class.
